transcript.content: Hello, and welcome. I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Doctor. Well, I guess what finally made me come in is that my neck, my shoulders, and my jaw are just tight almost all the time now. It feels like I'm constantly bracing for bad news, you know? Even when there's nothing going on and I'm just sitting at my desk at school, or trying to watch TV at night, I'm just completely tensed up.
When you notice your neck and shoulders getting tight, do you find that you're worried or anxious about something at that moment, or does the tension just seem to happen on its own?

Well, it's definitely tied to what I'm thinking about. I mean, my mind just doesn't stop. When I notice the tension, it's usually because I'm worrying about... well, a dozen things at once. 

My mind just keeps jumping from one thing to another. Like, I'll be stressing over whether the contractors missed something working on the house, and then suddenly I'm worried that my lesson plans are slipping. Then I start thinking about the robotics kids at school and whether they're falling behind. And... I guess it all just builds up to this constant worry that I'm disappointing my wife and my family by not keeping everything perfectly under control. So, yeah, the tightness is definitely connected to all that worrying.
Over the past few months, would you say that you're feeling this constant worry and tension on most days of the week, or is it more on and off?

It's definitely most days. Actually, pretty much every day. It's been going on for about seven months now. That's when a pipe burst at our house, and the remodeling just... threw everything into chaos. Since then, it's just been a constant thing.
Have you ever had times when the anxiety suddenly spikes and becomes really intense very quickly—like a sudden wave of panic or dread that feels overwhelming—even if just for a few minutes?

No, I haven't really had anything like that. It's not a sudden spike or a wave of panic, it's just... it's just always there. A steady, constant kind of worry that just hums in the background all day. But no sudden, intense panic attacks or anything like that.
When you're having these worries, do you feel like you can control them or stop them, or does the worry just keep going even when you try to push it away?

I can't really control them, no. I mean, I try. I'll tell myself to just stop and focus on the class in front of me. But then one small thought pops into my head—like a late invoice for the house, or a student falling behind—and it just sets off this whole chain of what-ifs. Once that starts, I just can't seem to shut it down, no matter how much I try to push it away.

You mentioned worrying about the house renovation, your lesson plans, and your students. Are there other areas of your life that you find yourself worrying about regularly—like your health, finances, relationships, or other things—or is most of your worry concentrated mainly on these work and home responsibilities?

It really just jumps around, honestly. I mean, it is a lot about the house and school, but it definitely bleeds into my family life, too. My mind just keeps jumping from... wondering if the contractors missed something in the house, to whether my lesson plans are slipping. Then I'll start stressing about whether the robotics kids are falling behind. And then... I just worry that I'm disappointing my wife and family by not keeping everything under control. So it just kind of cycles through all of that, all day.

How much has this constant worry been affecting your ability to do your job as a teacher, or your relationships with your wife and family? Has it made it hard for you to concentrate, sleep, or enjoy things you normally would?

It's definitely affecting things. I mean, at work, I've started falling behind on my lesson prep and grading, which isn't like me. It's just hard to focus. And outside of work... well, I usually manage some things for the local community theater, but I actually had to give up parts of that recently. I just couldn't keep up with all of it anymore with my mind constantly spinning.

Besides the muscle tension in your neck and shoulders, have you noticed other physical symptoms—like feeling restless or on edge, getting tired easily, having trouble concentrating, or feeling irritable—as part of this constant worry?

Yeah, I definitely feel restless. I'm just... wound up most of the day, honestly. It feels like I'm always waiting for something else to go wrong. I actually catch myself pacing around the classroom a lot. And between periods, I'm constantly checking my phone for messages from the contractor. I just feel really on edge and can't seem to sit still.

inference_history.note: Initial presentation with persistent muscle tension (neck, shoulders, jaw) and subjective sense of anticipatory worry ('bracing for bad news'). This suggests anxiety disorder with prominent somatic symptoms. F41.1 (Generalized Anxiety Disorder) is primary given the constant tension and worry. F41.9 (Anxiety disorder unspecified) and F43.10 (Post-traumatic stress disorder, single episode) included pending trauma history. F45.9 (Somatoform disorder unspecified) and F48.9 (Unspecified nonorganic mental disorder) included due to prominent physical symptoms.
